children.text: jyākṛṣṭibaddhakhaṭakāmukhapāṇipṛṣṭhapreṅkhannakhāṃśucayasaṃvalito 'mbikāyāḥ
children.translated_text: May the sidelong glance of <s>Ambikā</s> protect you: it is encircled by clusters of rays from her quivering nails on the backs of her hands, whose bracelets are fastened as she draws the bowstring to the notch of the arrow.

children.text: tvāṃ pātu mañjaritapallavakarṇapūralobhabhramadbhramaravibhramabhṛt kaṭākṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That glance bears the graceful illusion of bees wandering in desire for the blossom-like leaf-shoots that fill her ears.

children.text: kṣipto hastāvalagnaḥ prasabham abhihato 'py ādadāno 'ṃśukāntaṃ gṛhṇan keśeṣvapāstaścaraṇanipatito nekṣitaḥ sambhrameṇa
children.translated_text: It was flung away though it clung to their hands; though struck by force, it seized the end of their garments; grasping their hair, it was thrust aside; fallen at their feet, it was not looked at in their agitation.

children.text: āliṅgan yo 'vadhūtas tripurayuvatibhiḥ sāśrunetrotpalābhiḥ kāmīvārdrāparādhaḥ sa dahatu duritaṃ śāmbhavo vaḥ śarāgniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though it embraced them, it was shaken off by the young women of <s>Tripura</s>, their lotus-eyes filled with tears; may that arrow-fire of <s>Śambhu</s>, like a lover damp with offense and passion, burn away your evil.

children.text: ālolām alakāvalīṃ vilulitāṃ bibhraccalatkuṇḍalaṃ kiṃcin mṛṣṭaviśeṣakaṃ tanutaraiḥ khedāmbhasāṃ śīkaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Her face, at the end of lovemaking, bore a tossing row of curls, was disheveled, had swinging earrings, and had its forehead mark slightly rubbed away by fine droplets of sweat.

children.text: tanvyā yat suratāntatāntanayanaṃ vaktraṃ rativyatyaye tattvāṃ pātu cirāya kiṃ hariharabrahmādibhirdaivataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After the reversal of love-play, that slender woman's face, with eyes wearied by the end of passion, may protect you for a long time; what need is there of deities such as <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>?

children.text: alasavalitaiḥ premārdrārdrair muhurmukulīkṛtaiḥ kṣaṇam abhimukhair lajjālolair nimeṣaparāṅmukhaiḥ
children.translated_text: With lazy, rolling glances, moist and tender with love, repeatedly half-closed, for a moment turned toward him, restless with shame, and turned away at the blink of an eye,

children.text: hṛdayanihitaṃ bhāvākūtaṃ vamadbhirivekṣaṇaiḥ kathaya sukṛtī ko 'yaṃ mugdhe tvayādya vilokyate ||
children.translated_text: with eyes that seem to pour out the hidden intention lodged in the heart, tell me, innocent girl: what fortunate man are you looking at today?

children.text: datto'syāḥ praṇayastvayaiva bhavatā ceyaṃ ciraṃ lālitā daivād adya kila tvameva kṛtavān asyā navaṃ vipriyam
children.translated_text: You yourself gave her your affection, and you yourself cherished her for a long time; now, by fate, you yourself have indeed done her this new injury.

children.text: manyurduḥsaha eṣa yātyupaśamaṃ no sāntvavādaiḥ sphuṭaṃ he nistraṃśa vimuktakaṇṭhakaruṇaṃ tāvatsakhī roditu ||
children.translated_text: This unbearable anger clearly does not grow calm with words of conciliation. O cruel man, let her friend first weep aloud with a throat released into pity.

children.text: likhannāste bhūmiṃ bahiravanataḥ prāṇadayito nirāhārāḥ sakhyaḥ satataruditocchūnanayanāḥ
children.translated_text: Outside, her beloved, dearer than life, sits bent down, scratching the ground; her friends, fasting, have eyes swollen from constant weeping.

children.text: parityaktaṃ sarvaṃ hasitapaṭhitaṃ pañjaraśukais tavāvasthā ceyaṃ visṛja kaṭhine mānamadhunā ||
children.translated_text: Even the cage-parrots have abandoned all their laughing and reciting. Such is your condition; hard-hearted girl, give up your pride now.

children.text: nāryastanvi haṭhāddharanti ramaṇaṃ tiṣṭhanti no vāritās tatkiṃ tāmyasi kiṃ ca rodiṣi mudhā tāsāṃ priyaṃ mā kṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: Women, slender one, forcibly carry off a lover and do not stop when restrained; so why do you pine, and why do you weep in vain? Do not do what pleases them.

children.text: kāntaḥ keliruciryuvā sahṛdayastādṛkpatiḥ kātare kiṃ no barkarakarkaraiḥ priyaśatairākramya vikrīyate ||
children.translated_text: Your beloved is playful, handsome, young, and tender-hearted; fearful girl, is such a husband not bought by trampling over hundreds of lovers harsh as gravel?

children.text: kopāt komalalolabāhulatikāpāśena baddhā dṛḍhaṃ nītvā keliniketanaṃ dayitayā sāyaṃ sakhīnāṃ puraḥ
children.translated_text: In anger, his beloved bound him fast with the noose of her tender, trembling creeper-like arms, led him at evening to the pleasure chamber before her friends,

children.text: bhūyo'pyevamiti skhalan mṛdugirā saṃsūcya duśceṣṭitaṃ dhanyo hanyata eva nihnutiparaḥ preyān rudatyā hasan ||
children.translated_text: and, as he stumbled out in a soft voice that he would do such mischief again, the blessed lover, intent on denial, was simply beaten while laughing as she wept.

children.text: praharaviratau madhye vāhnastato'pi pare'thavā kimuta sakale jāte vāhṇi priya tvamihaiṣyasi
children.translated_text: Will you come here, beloved, at the end of the first watch, or in the middle of the day, or after that? Or only when the whole day has passed?

children.text: iti dinaśataprāpyaṃ deśaṃ priyasya yiyāsato harati gamanaṃ bālālāpaiḥ sabāṣpagalajjalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With such girlish talk, her throat choked with tears and shame, she prevents the departure of her lover, who wishes to go to a land reached only after a hundred days.

children.text: yātāḥ kiṃ na milanti sundari punaścintā tvayā matkṛte no kāryā nitarāṃ kṛśāmi kathayatyevaṃ sabāṣpe mayi
children.translated_text: 'Those who have gone do not meet again, beautiful one; you must not worry on my account. I am growing extremely thin,' I said with tears.

children.text: lajjāmantharatārakeṇa nipataddhārāśruṇā cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭvā māṃ hasitena bhāvimaraṇotsāhastayā sūcitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Looking at me with an eye whose pupil was slowed by shame and from which streams of tears were falling, she indicated by a smile her readiness for the death that was to come.

children.text: dhīraṃ vāridharasya vāri kirataḥ śrutvā niśīthe dhvaniṃ dīrghocchvāsamudaśruṇā virahiṇīṃ bālāṃ ciraṃ dhyāyatā
children.translated_text: At midnight, hearing the sound of a rain-cloud steadily pouring water, he thought long of the young woman separated from him, sighing deeply and shedding tears.

children.text: adhvanyena vimuktakaṇṭhamakhilāṃ rātriṃ tathā kranditaṃ grāmīṇairvrajato janasya vasatirgrāme niṣiddhā yathā ||
children.translated_text: Then, on the road, he wailed aloud the whole night so much that the villagers forbade lodging in the village to people traveling on the road.

children.text: kathamapi sakhi krīḍākopād vrajeti mayodite kaṭhinahṛdayastyaktvā śayyāṃ balād gata eva saḥ
children.translated_text: Somehow, friend, when in playful anger I said, 'Go away,' that hard-hearted man left the bed and went off by force.

children.text: iti sarabhasaṃ dhvastapremṇi vyapetaghṛṇe jane punarapi hatavrīḍaṃ cetaḥ prayāti karomi kim ||
children.translated_text: Though that man was so impetuously destructive of love and devoid of pity, my shameless heart goes back to him again; what am I to do?

children.text: dampatyorniśi jalpatorgṛhaśukenākarṇitaṃ yadvacas tatprātargurusaṃnidhau nigadatastasyopahāraṃ vadhūḥ
children.translated_text: What the husband and wife said while chatting at night was overheard by the house-parrot; when it began to repeat it in the morning in the elders' presence, the bride,

children.text: karṇālaṃkṛtipadmarāgaśakalaṃ vinyasya cañcūpuṭe vrīḍārtā prakaroti dāḍimaphalavyājena vāgbandhanam ||
children.translated_text: tormented by shame, placed in the hollow of its beak a fragment of ruby from her ear ornament, and, under the pretext of a pomegranate seed, stopped its speech as a gift.

children.text: ajñānena parāṅmukhīṃ paribhavād āśliṣya māṃ duḥkhitāṃ kiṃ labdhaṃ caṭula tvayeha nayatā saubhāgyametāṃ daśām
children.translated_text: Through ignorance you embraced me, who was turned away and distressed by humiliation. Fickle one, what have you gained here by bringing your good fortune to this state?

children.text: paśyaitad dayitākucavyatikaronmṛṣṭāṅgarāgāruṇaṃ vakṣaste malatailapaṅkaśabalair veṇīpadairaṅkitam ||
children.translated_text: Look: your chest is red where the body-paint was rubbed off by contact with your beloved's breasts, and it is marked by streaks from her braid, mottled with the mud of mālatī oil.

children.text: ekatrāsanasaṃsthitiḥ parihatā pratyudgamād dūratas tāmbūlānayanacchalena rabhasāśleṣo'pi saṃvighnitaḥ
children.translated_text: Sitting on the same seat was avoided; greeting him from afar, even a sudden embrace under the pretext of bringing betel was obstructed.

children.text: ālāpo'pi na miśritaḥ parijanaṃ vyāpārayantyāntike kāntaṃ pratyupacārataścaturayā kopaḥ kṛtārthīkṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even conversation was not joined, as she kept attendants busy nearby; through formal courtesy toward her beloved, the clever woman made her anger successful.

children.text: dṛṣṭvaikāsanasaṃsthite priyatame paścād upetyādarād ekasyā nayane pidhāya vihitakrīḍānubandhacchalaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing his beloved seated on one seat with another woman, the rogue came up from behind with deference and, covering one woman's eyes, made a pretext of continuing a game.

children.text: īṣadvakrimakaṃdharaḥ sapulakaḥ premollasanmānasām antarhāsalasatkapolaphalakāṃ dhūrto'parāṃ cumbati ||
children.translated_text: With his neck slightly crooked, his hair bristling, and his mind swelling with love, he kissed the other woman, whose cheeks shone with an inward smile.

children.text: caraṇapatanapratyākhyānātprasādaparāṅmukhe nibhṛtakitavācāretyuktvā ruṣā paruṣīkṛte
children.translated_text: When her lover's falling at her feet was rejected, when she was turned away from appeasement, and when, in anger, she harshly called him a secret deceiver in conduct,

children.text: vrajati ramaṇe niḥśvasyoccaiḥ stanasthitahastayā nayanasalilacchannā dṛṣṭiḥ sakhīṣu niveśitā ||
children.translated_text: as he went away, she sighed deeply, placed her hand on her breast, and fixed upon her friends a gaze veiled with tears.

children.text: kāñcyā gāḍhatarāvaruddhavasanaprāntā kimarthaṃ punar mugdhākṣī svapitīti tatparijanaṃ svairaṃ priye pṛcchati
children.translated_text: When the beloved freely asks her attendants, "Why, again, has the doe-eyed girl gone to sleep, with the edge of her garment held so tightly by her girdle?"

children.text: mātaḥ svaptumapīha vārayati māmityāhitakrodhayā paryasya svapiticchalena śayane datto'vakāśastayā ||
children.translated_text: then she, in pretended anger, says, "Mother, he prevents me even from sleeping here," and, turning over as if to sleep, gives him room on the bed.

children.text: ekasmiñśayane parāṅmukhatayā vītottaraṃ tāmyator anyonyasya hṛdi sthite'pyanunaye saṃrakṣatorgauravam
children.translated_text: On a single bed, turned away from one another, endlessly pining, though conciliation lies in each other's heart, both preserving their dignity,

children.text: dampatyoḥ śanakairapāṅgavalanān miśrībhavaccakṣuṣor bhagno mānakaliḥ sahāsarabhasaṃ vyāsaktakaṇṭhagraham ||
children.translated_text: for the husband and wife, as their eyes slowly mingle through sidelong glances, the quarrel of pride is broken, with laughter and sudden eagerness, in a tight embrace around the neck.

children.text: paśyāmo mayi kiṃ prapadyata iti sthairyaṃ mayālambitaṃ kiṃ māmālapatītyayaṃ khalu śaṭhaḥ kopastayāpyāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: "Let us see what she will do toward me"; thus I had assumed firmness. "Will this rogue speak to me?"; she too had taken refuge in anger.

children.text: ityanyonyavilakṣadṛṣṭicature tasminnavasthāntare savyājaṃ hasitaṃ mayā dhṛtiharo bāṣpastu muktastayā ||
children.translated_text: In that changed state, clever with mutually embarrassed glances, I smiled with a pretext; but she shed tears that stole away my composure.

children.text: parimlāne māne mukhaśaśini tasyāḥ karadhṛte mayi kṣīṇopāye praṇipatanamātraikaśaraṇe
children.translated_text: When her pride had faded, and her moon-face was held in my hand, when my means were exhausted and my only refuge was mere prostration,

children.text: tayā pakṣmaprāntavrajapuṭaniruddhena sahasā prasādo bāṣpena stanataṭaviśīrṇena kathitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then her favor was suddenly declared by tears, held back within the hollows at the edges of her eyelashes, and then scattered over the slope of her breasts.

children.text: tasyāḥ sāndravilepanastanataṭapraśleṣamudrāṅkitaṃ kiṃ vakṣaścaraṇānativyatikaravyājena gopāyate
children.translated_text: "Why is your chest, marked with the seal of contact with the edge of her breasts thick with ointment, being hidden under the pretext of bowing at her feet?"

children.text: ityukte kva tad ityudīrya sahasā tatsampramārṣṭuṃ mayā sāśliṣṭā rabhasena tatsukhavaśāttanvyāpi tad vismṛtam ||
children.translated_text: When this was said, I exclaimed, "Where is that?" and, in haste to wipe it off, embraced her impetuously; overpowered by that pleasure, the slender girl too forgot it.

children.text: tvaṃ mugdhākṣi vinaiva kañculikayā dhatse manohāriṇīṃ lakṣmīmityabhidhāyini priyatame tadvīṭikāṃ saṃspṛśi
children.translated_text: "Doe-eyed girl, even without a bodice you possess a captivating beauty," said her beloved, touching her betel-box.

children.text: śayyopāntaniviṣṭasasmitamukhīnetrotsavānandito niryātaḥ śanakairalīkavacanopanyāsam ālījanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the attendant women, who had been sitting at the edge of the bed with smiling faces and delighting in the festival for their eyes, slowly went out on the pretext of that false remark.

children.text: bhrūbhaṅge racite'pi dṛṣṭiradhikaṃ sotkaṇṭham udvīkṣate kārkaśyaṃ gamite'pi cetasi tanūromāñcamālambate
children.translated_text: Even when a frown has been formed, the gaze looks up with still greater longing; even when hardness has been brought into the mind, her body takes on horripilation.

children.text: ruddhāyāmapi vāci sasmitamidaṃ dagdhānanaṃ jāyate dṛṣṭe nirvahaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati kathaṃ mānasya tasmiñjane ||
children.translated_text: Even when speech is restrained, this accursed face begins to smile: when that man is seen, how will the performance of pride be carried through?

children.text: kānte katyapi vāsarāṇi gamaya tvaṃ mīlayitvā dṛśau svasti svasti nimīlayāmi nayane yāvan na śūnyā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: "Beloved, pass a few days with your eyes closed." "Farewell, farewell; I shall close my eyes only while the quarters are not empty."

children.text: āyātā vayamāgamiṣyati suhṛdvargasya bhāgyodayaiḥ saṃdeśo vada kastavābhilaṣitastīrtheṣu toyāñjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I have come; a message will arrive through the good fortune of your circle of friends. Tell me, what do you desire?" "A handful of water for me at the sacred bathing places."

children.text: sā patyuḥ prathamāparādhasamaye sakhyopadeśaṃ vinā no jānāti savibhramāṅgavalanāvakroktisaṃsūcanam
children.translated_text: At the time of her husband's first offense, without instruction from a friend, she does not know how to indicate it by coquettish turns of the body and crooked speech.

children.text: svacchairacchakapolamūlagalitaiḥ paryastanetrotpalā bālā kevalameva roditi luṭhallolālakairaśrubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The young girl merely weeps, with her eye-lotuses overturned and with clear tears falling from the roots of her bright cheeks, while her restless curls roll about.

children.text: bhavatu viditaṃ chadmālāpairalaṃ priya gamyatāṃ tanurapi na te doṣo'smākaṃ vidhistu parāṅmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: "Let it be known. Enough of deceptive talk, beloved; go. Your body is not at fault, nor are we; fate alone is turned away."

children.text: tava yathā tathābhūtaṃ prema prapannamimāṃ daśāṃ prakṛticapale kā naḥ pīḍā gate hatajīvite ||
children.translated_text: "Since your love, just as it is, has come to this condition, what pain remains for us, fickle by nature, when our wretched life has departed?"

children.text: urasi nihitastāro hāraḥ kṛtā jaghane ghane kalakalavatī kāñcī pādau kvaṇanmaṇinūpurau
children.translated_text: A brilliant necklace has been set upon your breast, a jingling girdle upon your broad hips, and jeweled anklets ringing upon your feet.

children.text: priyam abhisarasyevaṃ mugdhe samāhataḍiṇḍimā yadi kimadhikatrāsotkampaṃ diśaḥ samudīkṣase ||
children.translated_text: When, naive girl, you go to meet your beloved in this way, as if with drums beaten all around, why do you look about the directions with such trembling from excessive fear?

children.text: prātaḥ prātarupāgatena janitā nirnidratā cakṣuṣor mandāyāṃ mayi gauravavyapagamād utpāditaṃ lāghavam
children.translated_text: "By coming every morning you have produced sleeplessness in my eyes; because respect has vanished toward foolish me, you have produced lightness."

children.text: kiṃ mugdhe na mayā kṛtaṃ ramaṇadhīrmuktā tvayā gamyatāṃ dusthaṃ tiṣṭhasi yacca pathyamadhunā kartāsmi tacchroṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: "What have I not done, naive girl? You have abandoned the thought of your lover; go. Since you stand here distressed, what is wholesome now I shall do; you will hear it."

children.text: sā bālā vayam apragalbhamanasaḥ sā strī vayaṃ kātarāḥ sā pīnonnatimatpayodharayugaṃ dhatte sakhedā vayam
children.translated_text: "She is a young girl, while we are of timid mind; she is a woman, while we are fearful. She bears a pair of full and high breasts, while we are distressed."

children.text: sākrāntā jaghanasthalena guruṇā gantuṃ na śaktā vayaṃ doṣairanyajanāśritairapaṭavo jātāḥ sma ityadbhutam ||
children.translated_text: "She is burdened with the weight of her hip-region and unable to go, while we, through faults belonging to others, have become incompetent. This is astonishing."

children.text: prasthānaṃ valayaiḥ kṛtaṃ priyasakhairajasraṃ gataṃ dhṛtyā na kṣaṇamāsitaṃ vyavasitaṃ cittena gantuṃ puraḥ
children.translated_text: Departure has been undertaken by the bracelets; the dear friends have gone constantly; fortitude has not sat still for even a moment; the mind has resolved to go ahead.

children.text: gantuṃ niścitacetasi priyatame sarve samaṃ prasthitā gantavye sati jīvitapriyasuhṛtsārthaḥ kimu tyajyate ||
children.translated_text: When the beloved has a mind fixed on going, all have set out together; when there is a place to go, is the caravan of life and dear friends to be abandoned?

children.text: saṃdaṣṭādharapallavā sacakitaṃ hastāgram ādhunvatī māmāmuñca śaṭheti kopavacanair ānartitabhrūlatā
children.translated_text: Biting the bud of her lower lip, waving the tip of her hand in alarm, and making her vine-like brows dance with angry words, "Do not touch me, rogue!"

children.text: śītkārāñcitalocanā sarabhasaṃ yaiścumbitā māninī prāptaṃ tairamṛtaṃ mudhaiva mathito mūḍhaiḥ suraiḥ sāgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who have kissed the proud woman impetuously, while her eyes are bent with sighing sounds, have obtained nectar; the foolish gods churned the ocean in vain.

children.text: supto'yaṃ sakhi supyatāmiti gatāḥ sakhyastato'nantaraṃ premāvāsitayā mayā saralayā nyastaṃ mukhaṃ tanmukhe
children.translated_text: "He is asleep, friend; let him sleep." So the friends went away. Immediately afterward, being simple and perfumed with love, I placed my face upon his face.

children.text: jñāte'līkanimīlane nayanayordhūrtasya romāñcato lajjāsīn mama tena sāpyapahṛtā tatkālayogyaiḥ kramaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the rogue's false closing of his eyes was recognized from the horripilation on his body, my bashfulness was present; but he stole that too from me by acts suited to that moment.

children.text: kopo yatra bhrūkuṭiracanā nigraho yatra maunaṃ yatrānyonyasmitamanunayo yatra dṛṣṭiḥ prasādaḥ
children.translated_text: Where anger is the drawing together of the brows, where restraint is silence, where mutual smiling is conciliation, where a glance is favor,

children.text: tasya premṇastad idamadhunā vaiṣamaṃ paśya jātaṃ tvaṃ pādānte luṭhasi nahi me manyumokṣaḥ khalāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: see now the disparity that has arisen in that love: you roll at my feet, yet there is no release of anger from me, wicked woman that I am.

children.text: sutanu jahihi kopaṃ paśya pādānataṃ māṃ na khalu tava kadācitkopa evaṃvidho'bhūt
children.translated_text: Slender-waisted one, give up your anger; look at me, bowed at your feet. Surely your anger has never before been of this kind.

children.text: iti nigadati nāthe tiryagāmīlitākṣyā nayanajalamanalpaṃ muktamuktaṃ na kiṃcit ||
children.translated_text: As her lord says this, from eyes half-closed and turned aside, abundant tears are released again and again, but not a word.

children.text: gāḍhāliṅganavāmanīkṛtakucaprodbhinnaromodgamā sāndrasneharasātirekavigalatśrīmannitambāmbarā
children.translated_text: Her breasts made small by a tight embrace, her hair standing up as they burst forth, her splendid hip-cloth slipping away through the excess of dense love's sap,

children.text: mā mā mānada māti māmalamiti kṣāmākṣarollāpinī suptā kiṃ nu mṛtā nu kiṃ manasi me līnā vilīnā nu kim ||
children.translated_text: murmuring in faint syllables, 'No, no, honored one, do not, do not do this to me,' has she fallen asleep, or is she dead, or has she dissolved into my mind, or vanished away?

children.text: paṭālagne patyau namayati mukhaṃ jātavinayā haṭhāśleṣaṃ vāñchatyapaharati gātrāṇi nibhṛtam
children.translated_text: When her husband touches her garment, she lowers her face, born to modesty; when he desires a forced embrace, she quietly draws her limbs away.

children.text: na śaknotyākhyātuṃ smitamukhasakhīdattanayanā hriyā tāmyatyantaḥ prathamaparihāse navavadhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: Unable to speak, with her eyes fixed on a smiling-faced friend, the new bride wastes inwardly with shame at the first jesting of love.

children.text: gate premābandhe praṇayabahumāne vigalite nivṛtte sadbhāve jana iva jane gacchati puraḥ
children.translated_text: When the bond of love has gone, when the high regard of affection has melted away, when goodwill has ceased, and one person goes before another as mere people do,

children.text: tad utprekṣyotprekṣya priyasakhi gatāṃstāṃśca divasān na jāne ko heturdalati śatadhā yan na hṛdayam ||
children.translated_text: then, looking back again and again, dear friend, at those days now gone, I do not know what cause keeps the heart from splitting into a hundred pieces.

children.text: ciravirahiṇor utkaṇṭhārtiślathīkṛtagātrayor navamiva jagaj jātaṃ bhūyaścirād abhinandatoḥ
children.translated_text: For the two long-separated lovers, their bodies loosened by the pain of longing, and greeting each other after a long time as if the world had become new again,

children.text: kathamapi dine dīrghe yāte niśāmadhirūḍhayoḥ prasarati kathā bahvī yūnor yathā na tathā ratiḥ ||
children.translated_text: when somehow the long day has passed and they have mounted the night, much conversation spreads between the young pair, but love-play does not spread in the same way.

children.text: dīrghā vandanamālikā viracitā hṛṣṭyaiva nendīvaraiḥ puṣpāṇāṃ prakaraḥ smitena racito no kundajātyādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: A long garland of homage was made with delight itself, not with blue lotuses; a mass of flowers was fashioned with her smile, not with jasmine and the like.

children.text: dattaḥ svedamucā payodharayuge nārghyo na kumbhāmbhasā svairevāvayavaiḥ priyasya viśatastanvyā kṛtaṃ maṅgalam ||
children.translated_text: An offering was given to the pair of breasts by sweat poured out there, not by water from a jar; with her own limbs the slender woman performed the auspicious rite for her beloved as he entered.

children.text: kānte sāgasi śāyite priyasakhīveśaṃ vidhāyāgate bhrāntyāliṅgya mayā rahasyamuditaṃ tatsaṅgamākāṅkṣayā
children.translated_text: When my beloved, though guilty, had lain down and then came back in the guise of my dear friend, I mistakenly embraced him, desiring that union, and joyfully told him a secret.

children.text: mugdhe duṣkarametad ityatitarāmuktvā sahāsaṃ balād āliṅgya chalitāsmi tena kitavenādya pradoṣāgame ||
children.translated_text: 'Innocent girl, this is hard to do,' he said, laughing greatly; then, forcibly embracing me, I was deceived today at the coming of evening by that rogue.

children.text: āśaṅkya praṇatiṃ paṭāntapihitau pādau karotyādarāt vyājenāgatamāvṛṇoti hasitaṃ na spaṣṭamudvīkṣate
children.translated_text: Expecting his prostration, she carefully hides her feet under the edge of her garment; when he comes by a pretext, she covers her smile and does not look straight at him.

children.text: mayyālāpavati pratīpavacanaṃ sakhyā sahābhāṣate tasyāstiṣṭhatu nirbharapraṇayitā māno'pi ramyodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When I speak, she gives contrary replies and talks with her friend. Let her deep affection stay as it is; even her anger has a lovely beginning.

children.text: sā yāvanti padānyalīkavacanairālījanaiḥ śikṣitā tāvantyeva kṛtāgaso drutataraṃ vyāhṛtya patyuḥ puraḥ
children.translated_text: All the words that the women friends had taught her with false statements, just so many she quickly uttered before her husband, who had committed an offense.

children.text: prārabdhā purato yathā manasijasyājñā tathā vartituṃ premṇo maugdhyavibhūṣaṇasya sahajaḥ ko'pyeṣa kāntaḥ kramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Before him she began to behave just as <s>Manasija</s>'s command required. This is some natural and lovely course of love, whose ornament is innocence.

children.text: dūrādutsukamāgate vivalitaṃ sambhāṣiṇi sphāritaṃ saṃśliṣyatyaruṇaṃ gṛhītavasane kiṃcin natabhrūlatam
children.translated_text: When the beloved came eagerly from afar, her eye turned away; when he spoke, it opened wide; when he embraced her, it grew red; when he seized her garment, her brow-creeper bent a little.

children.text: māninyāścaraṇānativyatikare bāṣpāmbupūrṇekṣaṇaṃ cakṣurjātamaho prapañcacaturaṃ jātāgasi preyasi ||
children.translated_text: At the moment when the proud woman had to bow to his feet, her eye filled with tear-water. Ah, when her beloved was guilty, her eye became skilled in the whole drama.

children.text: aṅgānāmatitānavaṃ kathamidaṃ kampaśca kasmātkuto mugdhe pāṇḍukapolamānanamiti prāṇeśvare pṛcchati
children.translated_text: 'Why is this extreme thinness of your limbs, why this trembling, and whence, innocent girl, this pale-cheeked face?' so her lord of life asks.

children.text: tanvyā sarvamidaṃ svabhāvajamiti vyāhṛtya pakṣmāntaravyāpī bāṣpabharastayā calitayā niḥśvasya mukto'nyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Saying, 'All this is natural for the slender woman,' she sighed, turned away, and released elsewhere the weight of tears spreading between her eyelashes.

children.text: purastanvyā gotraskhalanacakito'haṃ natamukhaḥ pravṛtto vailakṣyātkimapi likhituṃ daivahatakaḥ
children.translated_text: Before the slender woman, startled by a slip in naming another lineage, I, with face bowed, began from embarrassment, ill-fated by destiny, to draw something.

children.text: sphuṭo rekhānyāsaḥ kathamapi sa tādṛk pariṇato gatā yena vyaktaṃ punaravayavaiḥ saiva taruṇī ||
children.translated_text: Somehow that clear tracing of lines turned out in such a way that, by its limbs, that very young woman manifestly appeared again.

children.text: kaṭhinahṛdaye muñca bhrāntiṃ vyalīkakathāśritāṃ piśunavacanair duḥkhaṃ netuṃ na yuktamimaṃ janam
children.translated_text: Hard-hearted girl, abandon the delusion resting on false tales. It is not right to bring this person to grief through the words of slanderers.

children.text: kimidamathavā satyaṃ mugdhe tvayā hi viniścitaṃ yad abhirucitaṃ tan me kṛtvā priye sukhamāsyatām ||
children.translated_text: Or perhaps this is true, innocent one, since you have firmly decided it. Beloved, do whatever pleases you toward me, and sit happily.

children.text: mandaṃ mudritapāṃśavaḥ paripatajjhaṅkārajhañjhāmarudvegadhvastakuṭīrakāntaragatacchidreṣu labdhāntarāḥ
children.translated_text: Slowly, their dust sealed down, entering through gaps made in the interiors of cottages shattered by the force of falling, roaring, stormy winds,

children.text: karmavyagrakuṭumbinīkucataṭasvedacchidaḥ prāvṛṣaḥ prārambhe nipatanti kandaladalollāsāḥ payobindavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the beginning of the rains, water-drops that gladden the leaves of kandala plants fall, cutting the sweat on the breasts of housewives busy with their work.

children.text: pītastuṣārakiraṇo madhunaiva sārdham antaḥ praviśya caṣake pratibimbavartī
children.translated_text: The moon, whose rays are cold, was drunk together with wine, having entered inside the cup while existing as a reflection.

children.text: mānāndhakāramapi mānavatījanasya nūnaṃ bibheda yad asau prasasāda sadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely it even pierced the darkness of pride in the proud woman, since she at once became gracious.

children.text: nabhasi jaladalakṣmīṃ sambhṛtāṃ vīkṣya diṣṭyā prasarasi yadi kāntetyardhamuktvā kathaṃcit
children.translated_text: Seeing, by good fortune, the splendor of clouds gathered in the sky, and somehow half saying, 'Beloved, if you go forth...',

children.text: mama paṭamavalambya prollikhantī dharitrīṃ tadanukṛtavatī sā yatra vāco nivṛttāḥ ||
children.translated_text: she, holding on to my garment and scratching the ground, imitated that place where words cease.

children.text: iyamasau taralāyatalocanā gurusamunnatapīnapayodharā
children.translated_text: This is she: that beloved of mine, with restless, wide eyes and with full breasts high and heavy,

children.text: pṛthunitambabharālasagāminī priyatamā mama jīvitahāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: with a broad weight of hips and a languid gait, the one who steals my life.

children.text: sālaktakena navapallavakomalena pādena nūpuravatā madanālasena
children.translated_text: He who is struck by his beloved, out of the offense of love, with a lac-dyed foot, tender as a new shoot, ankleted, and languid with passion,

children.text: yastāḍyate dayitayā praṇayārādhāt so'ṅgīkṛto bhagavatā makaradhvajena ||
children.translated_text: that man has been accepted by the blessed <s>Makaradhvaja</s>.

children.text: bāle nātha vimuñca mānini ruṣaṃ roṣān mayā kiṃ kṛtaṃ khedo'smāsu na me'parādhyati bhavān sarve'parādhā mayi
children.translated_text: 'Girl, my lord, let go; proud woman, give up your anger.' 'What have I done in anger?' 'There is no fault in me against us.' 'Sir, you do no wrong; all offenses are in me.'

children.text: tatkiṃ rodiṣi gadgadena vacasā kasyāgrato rudyate nanvetan mama kā tavāsmi dayitā nāsmītyato rudyate ||
children.translated_text: Then why do you weep? With a voice choked by sobs, before whom is one to weep? 'Surely this is mine.' 'What am I to you, beloved?' 'You are not mine'--for that reason she weeps.

children.text: nītvoccairvikṣipantaḥ kṛtatuhinakaṇāsārasaṅgān parāgān kaundān ānanditālīn atitarasurabhīn bhūriśo diṅmukheṣu
children.translated_text: Carrying off the pollen of white lotuses, loudly scattering it, joined with showers of icy drops, delighting the bees, exceedingly fragrant, again and again toward the quarters,

children.text: ete te kuṅkumāktastanakalaśabharāsphālanād ucchalantaḥ pītvā śītkārivaktraṃ śiśuharidṛśāṃ haimanā vānti vātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these winter winds blow after drinking in the sighing mouths of young doe-eyed women, as they leap up from the striking of breasts heavy as jars and smeared with saffron.

children.text: śrutvā tanvyā niśīthe navaghanarasitaṃ viślathāṅkaṃ patitvā śayyāyāṃ bhūmipṛṣṭhe karataladhṛtayā duḥkhitālījanena
children.translated_text: At midnight, hearing the deep rumbling of a fresh cloud, she fell from the bed, her embrace loosened, onto the surface of the ground; by her distressed friends she was held in their hands.

children.text: sotkaṇṭhaṃ muktakaṇṭhaṃ kaṭhinakucataṭāghātaśīrṇāśrubindu smṛtvā smṛtvā priyasya skhalitamṛduvaco rudyate pānthavadhvā ||
children.translated_text: The traveler's wife weeps with longing, with her throat opened in loud lament, remembering again and again the soft, stumbling words of her beloved, while her tears are shattered by blows against the hard slopes of her breasts.

children.text: śliṣṭaḥ kaṇṭhe kimiti na mayā mūḍhayā prāṇanāthaś cumbatyasmin vadanavidhutiḥ kiṃ kṛtā kiṃ na dṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Why did I, foolish woman, not clasp my lord of life around the neck? When he was kissing me, why did I shake away my face? Why did I not look at him?

children.text: noktaḥ kasmād iti navavadhūceṣṭitaṃ cintayantī paścāttāpaṃ vahati taruṇī premṇi jāte rasajñā ||
children.translated_text: Why did I not speak?' Thinking over the behavior of a new bride, the young woman, now skilled in love after love has arisen, bears remorse.

children.text: śrutvā nāmāpi yasya sphuṭaghanapulakaṃ jāyate'ṅgaṃ samantāt dṛṣṭvā yasyānanenduṃ bhavati vapuridaṃ candrakāntānukāri
children.translated_text: At the mere hearing of his name, whose body is everywhere covered with clearly swelling horripilation, and on seeing whose moon-like face this body becomes like a moonstone,

children.text: tasminnāgatya kaṇṭhagrahaṇasarabhasasthāyini prāṇanāthe bhagnā mānasya cintā bhavati mama punarvajramayyāḥ kadā nu ||
children.translated_text: when that lord of my life comes and remains impetuously clasping my neck, when, indeed, will the thought of pride be broken in me, hard as diamond?

children.text: rāmāṇāṃ ramaṇīyavaktraśaśinaḥ svedodabindupluto vyālolālakavallarīṃ pracalayan dhunvan nitambāmbaram
children.translated_text: In spring, at dawn, the wind blows over women whose charming face-moons are sprinkled with drops of sweat, stirring their restless creeper-like curls and shaking the garments at their hips;

children.text: prātarvāti madhau prakāmavikasadrājīvarājīrajo jālāmodamanoharo ratirasaglāniṃ haranmārutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is lovely with the fragrance of masses of pollen from rows of lotuses fully opening, and it removes the languor born from the flavor of love-play.

children.text: aṅgaṃ candanapāṇḍupallavamṛdustāmbūlatāmrādharo dhārāyantrajalābhiṣekakaluṣe dhautāñjane locane
children.translated_text: The body is pale with sandal and soft as a young leaf, the lips red with betel; the eyes, their collyrium washed away, are clouded by the sprinkling from water-jets;

children.text: antaḥpuṣpasugandhirārdrakavarī sarvāṅgalagnāmbaraṃ romāṇāṃ ramaṇīyatāṃ vidadhati grīṣmāparāhvāgame ||
children.translated_text: the wet hair is fragrant within from flowers, and the garment clings to every limb; at the arrival of a summer afternoon these things create the loveliness of the body's hairs standing erect.

children.text: varamasau divaso na punarniśā nanu niśaiva varaṃ na punardivā
children.translated_text: Better that day, not night again. No, better night itself, not day again.

children.text: ubhayametad upaitvathavā kṣayaṃ priyajanena na yatra samāgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or let both of these come to destruction, where there is no meeting with the beloved person.

children.text: lolairlocanavāribhiḥ saśapathaiḥ pādapraṇāmaiḥ priyair anyāstā vinivārayanti kṛpaṇāḥ prāṇeśvaraṃ prasthitam
children.translated_text: Other poor women stop their lord of life as he sets out with unsteady streams of tears from their eyes, with oaths, with prostrations at his feet, and with endearments.

children.text: puṇyāhaṃ vraja maṅgalaṃ sudivasaṃ prātaḥ prayātasya te yatsnehocitamīhitaṃ priyatama tvaṃ nirgataḥ śroṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: But I am fortunate: 'Go; may it be auspicious. May the morning of your departure be a blessed day. Beloved, once you have gone, you will hear what conduct is proper to affection.'

children.text: lagnā nāṃśukapallave bhujalatā na dvāradeśe 'rpitā no vā pādatale tayā nipatitaṃ tiṣṭheti noktaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Her creeper-like arm was not fastened to the hem of his garment, nor placed at the doorway; she did not fall at his feet, nor did she say the word 'Stay.'

children.text: kāle kevalamambudātimaline gantuṃ pravṛttaḥ śaṭhaḥ tanvyā bāṣpajalaughakalpitanadīpūreṇa baddhaḥ priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the rogue began to go at a time darkened by clouds alone, the slender woman bound her beloved with a flood like a river made from torrents of tear-water.

children.text: na jāne saṃmukhāyāte priyāṇi vadati priye
children.translated_text: I do not know, when my beloved comes before me and speaks dear words,

children.text: sarvāṇyaṅgāni me yānti śrotratāṃ kimu netratām ||
children.translated_text: whether all my limbs become ears or rather eyes.

children.text: virahaviṣamaḥ kāmo vāmastanuṃ kurute tanuṃ divasagaṇanādakṣaścāsau vyapetaghṛṇo yamaḥ
children.translated_text: Love, harsh through separation and perverse, makes the slender body slenderer; and this <s>Yama</s>, skilled at counting days and devoid of pity,

children.text: tvamapi vaśago mānavyādhervicintaya nātha he kisalayamṛdur jīved evaṃ kathaṃ pramadājanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: you too, lord, are under the control of the disease of pride. Consider: how can womankind, tender as a leaf-shoot, live in such a state?

children.text: pādāsakte suciramiha te vāmatā kaiva kānte sanmārgasthe praṇayini jane kopane ko'parādhaḥ
children.translated_text: Beloved, while she has long clung here to your feet, what perverseness can there be? When a loving person stands on the good path, what offense is there in one who is angry?

children.text: itthaṃ tasyāḥ parijanakathā kopavegopaśāntau bāṣpodbhedais tadanu sahasā na sthitaṃ na prayātam ||
children.translated_text: Thus spoke her attendants; when the force of her anger subsided, then, because tears burst forth, she neither stayed nor went away at once.

children.text: purābhūdasmākaṃ niyatamavibhinnā tanuriyaṃ tato nu tvaṃ preyānvayamapi hatāśāḥ priyatamāḥ
children.translated_text: Formerly this body of ours was surely undivided; after that you became the lover, and we too, hopeless women, became beloveds.

children.text: idānīṃ nāthastvaṃ vayamapi kalatraṃ kimaparaṃ mayāptaṃ prāṇānāṃ kuliśakaṭhinānāṃ phalamidam ||
children.translated_text: Now you are the lord, and we too are the wife. What more is there? This is the fruit I have obtained from my lives, hard as thunderbolts.

children.text: mugdhe mugdhatayaiva netumakhilaḥ kālaḥ kimārabhyate mānaṃ dhatsva dhṛtiṃ badhāna ṛjutāṃ dūre kuru preyasi
children.translated_text: Simple girl, are you beginning to spend all your time in mere simplicity? Bear pride, fasten on firmness, put straightforwardness far away, beloved.

children.text: sakhyaivaṃ pratibodhitā prativacastāmāha bhītānanā nīcaiḥ śaṃsa hṛdi sthito nanu sa me prāṇeśvaraḥ śroṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Thus instructed by her friend, she, with a frightened face, answered her: 'Speak softly; surely that lord of my life is lodged in my heart and will hear.'

children.text: pīto yataḥ prabhṛti kāmapipāsitena tasyā mayādhararasaḥ pracuraḥ priyāyāḥ
children.translated_text: From the moment when, thirsty with desire, I drank the abundant flavor of the lip of that beloved woman,

children.text: tṛṣṇā tataḥ prabhṛti me dviguṇatvameti lāvaṇyamasti bahu tatra kimapi citram ||
children.translated_text: from that moment my thirst has grown double. There is much beauty there; what wonder is there in it?

children.text: kva prasthitāsi karabhoru ghane niśīthe prāṇādhiko vasati yatra janaḥ priyo me
children.translated_text: Where are you going, elephant-thighed girl, in the deep midnight? 'Where the person dearer than life to me dwells.'

children.text: ekākinī vada kathaṃ na bibheṣi bāle nanvasti puṅkhitaśaro madanaḥ sahāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, child, how are you not afraid, all alone? 'Is not <s>Madana</s>, with his feathered arrows, my companion?'

children.text: līlātāmarasāhato 'nyavanitāniḥśaṅkadaṣṭādharaḥ kaścitkesaradūṣitekṣaṇa iva vyāmīlya netre sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: A certain man, struck by a playful lotus and with his lip fearlessly bitten by another woman, stood with eyes closed, as though his eye had been stained with pollen.

children.text: mugdhā kuḍmalitānanena dadhato vāyuṃ sthitā tasya sā bhrāntyā dhūrtatayā ca vepathumatī tenāniśaṃ cumbitā ||
children.translated_text: The innocent girl, with bud-like face, stood blowing upon him; trembling both from confusion and from his cunning, she was kissed by him continually.

children.text: sphuṭatu hṛdayaṃ kāmaṃ kāmaṃ karotu tanuṃ tanuṃ na sakhi caṭulapremṇā kāryaṃ punardayitena me
children.translated_text: Let the heart split as it wishes; let passion make the body as thin as it wishes. Friend, I have no more business with a beloved whose love is fickle.

children.text: iti sarabhasaṃ mānāṭopād udīrya vacastayā ramaṇapadavī sāraṅgākṣyā saśaṅkitamīkṣitā ||
children.translated_text: After the doe-eyed woman had uttered these words impetuously in the pomp of pride, she looked anxiously toward the path of her lover.

children.text: gāḍhāśleṣaviśīrṇacandanarajaḥpuñjaprakarṣādiyaṃ śayyā samprati komalāṅgi paruṣetyāropya māṃ vakṣasi
children.translated_text: Placing me upon her breast, the soft-limbed girl said, "This bed is now rough, because the heaps of sandal powder have been scattered by tight embraces,"

children.text: gāḍhauṣṭhagrahapūrvamākulatayā pādāgrasaṃdaṃśakenākṛṣyāmbaramātmano yaducitaṃ dhūrtena tatprastutam ||
children.translated_text: and, after first seizing my lips firmly, in her agitation she pulled at her own garment with the bite of her toe-tips: whatever was proper was then begun by that rogue.

children.text: kathamapi kṛtapratyākhyāne priye skhalitottare virahakṛśayā kṛtvā vyājaṃ prakalpitamaśrutaṃ
children.translated_text: When her beloved had somehow been rejected and, as he answered, had faltered, she, emaciated by separation, made the pretext that she had not heard what had been said.

children.text: asahanasakhīśrotraprāptipramādasasaṃbhramaṃ vigalitadṛśā śūnye gehe samucchvasitaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, in sudden alarm lest the mistake should reach the ears of her intolerant friends, with eyes melting, she again sighed deeply in the empty house.

children.text: ā dṛṣṭiprasarāt priyasya padavīmudvīkṣya nirviṇṇayā vicchinneṣu pathiṣvahaḥpariṇatau dhvānte samutsarpati
children.translated_text: With weariness she watched her beloved's path as far as her sight could reach; when the roads had disappeared, the day had ended, and darkness was creeping up,

children.text: dattaikaṃ saśucā gṛhaṃ prati padaṃ pānthastriyāsminkṣaṇe mā bhūdāgata ityamandavalitagrīvaṃ punarvīkṣitam ||
children.translated_text: the traveler's wife, grieving, took a single step toward the house, but at that very moment looked back again with her neck strongly turned, thinking, "May he not have come?"

children.text: āyāte dayite manorathaśatairnītvā kathaṃciddinaṃ vaidagdhyāpagamājjaḍe parijane dīrghāṃ kathāṃ kurvati
children.translated_text: When her beloved had arrived, after she had somehow passed the day with hundreds of hopes, and when the dull attendants, having lost their cleverness, were telling a long story,

children.text: daṣṭāsmītyabhidhāya satvarapadaṃ vyādhūya cīnāṃśukaṃ tanvaṅgyā ratikātareṇa manasā nītaḥ pradīpaḥ śamam ||
children.translated_text: the slender girl, her mind distressed by passion, said, "I have been bitten," quickly shook her Chinese silk garment, and put out the lamp.

children.text: ālambyāṅgaṇavāṭikāparisare cūtadrume mañjarīṃ sarpatsāndraparāgalampaṭaraṇadbhṛṅgāṅganāśobhinīm
children.translated_text: Leaning on a mango tree at the edge of the courtyard garden, on a blossom-cluster made lovely by female bees humming greedily as they crept through its dense pollen,

children.text: manye svāṃ tanumuttarīyaśakalenācchādya bālā sphuratkaṇṭhadhvānanirodhakampitakucaśvāsodgamā roditi ||
children.translated_text: I think the young girl, covering her own body with a strip of upper garment, is weeping, her breasts trembling as she restrains the rising sound in her throat and her breath comes out.

children.text: yāsyāmiti samudyatasya gaditaṃ viśrabdham ākarṇitaṃ gacchandūramupekṣito muhurasau vyāvṛtya tiṣṭhannapi
children.translated_text: When he was ready to leave, she confidently heard him say, "I shall go." As he went far away, she ignored him again and again, though he turned back and stood still.

children.text: tacchūnye punarāsthitāsmi bhavane prāṇāsta ete dṛḍhāḥ sakhyastiṣṭhata jīvitavyasaninī dambhādahaṃ rodimi ||
children.translated_text: Now I am again staying in this house emptied of him; these life-breaths are hard indeed. Stay, friends: I, addicted to living, weep only from pretence.

children.text: śūnyaṃ vāsagṛhaṃ vilokya śayanādutthāya kiṃcicchanair nidrāvyājamupāgatasya suciraṃ nirvarṇya patyurmukham
children.translated_text: Seeing the bedchamber empty, she rose from the bed somewhat slowly; then, after long gazing at the face of her husband, who had approached under the pretext of sleep,

children.text: viśrabdhaṃ paricumbya jātapulakāmālokya gaṇḍasthalīṃ lajjānamramukhī priyeṇa hasatā bālā ciraṃ cumbitā ||
children.translated_text: the young girl kissed him trustingly. When her cheek was seen bristling with horripilation, she lowered her face in shame, while her smiling beloved kissed her for a long time.

children.text: loladbhrūlatayā vipakṣadigupanyāse'vadhūtaṃ śiras tadvṛttāntanirīkṣaṇe kṛtanamaskāro vilakṣaḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: When the direction of her rival was mentioned, she shook her head with her creeper-like brows quivering; when the affair was being examined, he stood embarrassed, with his respectful bow made.

children.text: kopāttāmrakapolabhittini mukhe dṛṣṭyā gataḥ pādayor utsṛṣṭo gurusannidhāvapi vidhirdvābhyāṃ na kālocitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On her face, whose cheek-walls were red with anger, his gaze went to her feet. Even in the presence of elders, the proper course for the occasion was abandoned by the two of them.

children.text: jātā notkalikā stanau na lulitau gātraṃ na romāñcitaṃ vaktraṃ svedakaṇānvitaṃ na sahasā yāvacchaṭhenāmunā
children.translated_text: No longing arose, her breasts did not tremble, her body did not bristle, nor did her face suddenly become covered with drops of sweat, until, by that rogue,

children.text: dṛṣṭenaiva mano hṛtaṃ dhṛtimuṣā prāṇeśvareṇādya me tatkenātra nirūpyamāṇanipuṇo mānaḥ samādhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: by my life-lord, thief of composure, merely being seen, my mind was stolen today. By what means, then, can pride, however skillfully considered, be maintained here?

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ kātaranetrayā cirataraṃ baddhāñjaliṃ yācitaḥ paścādaṃśukapallavena vidhṛto nirvyājamāliṅgitaḥ
children.translated_text: He was looked at for a long time with frightened eyes, begged with folded hands, then held back by the hem of the garment, and embraced without pretence.

children.text: ityākṣipya yadā samastamaghṛṇo gantuṃ pravṛttaḥ śaṭhaḥ pūrvaṃ prāṇaparigraho dayitayā muktastato vallabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When, after rejecting all this, the pitiless rogue began to go away, first the beloved was released by his dear one, but then her own hold on life was released.

children.text: kṛto dūrādeva smitamadhuramabhyudgamavidhiḥ śirasyājñā nyastā prativacanavatyānatimati
children.translated_text: From far away she performed a sweet-smiling rite of welcome; his command was placed upon her head by one who answered and bowed low.

children.text: na dṛṣṭeḥ śaithilyaṃ milana iti ceto dahati me nigūḍhāntaḥkopāt kaṭhinahṛdaye saṃvṛtiriyam ||
children.translated_text: Yet there was no slackening of her gaze at the meeting. This restraint, born from anger hidden within, burns my heart, hard-hearted woman though she is.

children.text: ekasmiñśayane vipakṣaramaṇīnāmagrahe mugdhayā sadyaḥ kopaparāṅmukhaṃ śayitayā cāṭūni kurvannapi
children.translated_text: On one bed, when the naive girl had turned away in instant anger at the mention of rival women, though her beloved kept speaking coaxing words,

children.text: āvegādavadhīritaḥ priyatamastūṣṇīṃ sthitastatkṣaṇāt mā bhūḥ supta ivaiṣa mandavalitagrīvaṃ punarvīkṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: she rejected him in agitation, and the lover instantly became silent; then she looked back again with her neck slightly turned, thinking, "May he not be like one asleep?"

children.text: malayamarutāṃ vātā yātā vikāsitamallikāparimalabharo bhagno grīṣmastvamutsahase yadi
children.translated_text: The winds of the Malaya breezes have passed; the weight of the fragrance of blossoming jasmine is broken; summer is gone. If you are able,

children.text: ghana ghaṭayituṃ niḥsnehaṃ tvāṃ ya eva nivartane prabhavati gavāṃ kiṃ naśchinnaṃ sa eva dhanañjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: cloud, unite yourself with this loveless one. The very <s>Dhanañjaya</s> who has power over the return of cattle: what has he cut off from us?

children.text: svaṃ dṛṣṭvā karajakṣataṃ madhumadakṣībā vicāryerṣyayā gacchantī kva nu gacchasīti vidhṛtā bālā paṭānte mayā
children.translated_text: Seeing her own nail-mark, intoxicated with spring wine, and reflecting with jealousy, the young girl was going away. I held her by the edge of her garment, saying, "Where are you going?"

children.text: pratyāvṛttamukhī sabāṣpanayanā māṃ muñca muñceti sā kopātprasphuritādharā yadavadattatkena vismaryate ||
children.translated_text: Turning her face back, with tear-filled eyes and lips trembling from anger, she said to me, "Let me go, let me go." By what could that be forgotten?

children.text: sālaktakaṃ śatadalādhikakāntiramyaṃ ratnaughadhāmanikarāruṇanūpuraṃ ca
children.translated_text: Lac-dyed, charming with a beauty surpassing a hundred-petalled lotus, and reddened by the mass of radiance from jewel-bright anklets,

children.text: kṣiptaṃ bhṛśaṃ kupitayā taralotpalākṣyā saubhāgyacihnamiva mūrdhni padaṃ vireje ||
children.translated_text: the foot flung forcefully by the very angry, tremulous-lotus-eyed girl shone upon my head like the mark of good fortune.

children.text: kapole patrālī karatalanirodhena mṛditā nipīto niḥśvāsairayamamṛtahṛdyo'dhararasaḥ
children.translated_text: The painted designs on your cheek have been rubbed away by the restraint of my palm; this lower-lip nectar, delightful as ambrosia, has been drunk by my sighs.

children.text: muhuḥ kaṇṭhe lagnas taralayati bāṣpaḥ stanataṭaṃ priyo manyurjātastava niranurodhe na tu vayam ||
children.translated_text: Again and again tears, clinging to your throat, shake the slope of your breasts. Your anger has become dear, since you show no indulgence, but we have not.

children.text: lākṣālakṣmalalāṭapaṭṭamabhitaḥ keyūramudrā gale vaktre kajjalakālimā nayanayos tāmbūlarāgo ghanaḥ
children.translated_text: A streak of lac on the band of the forehead, marks of armlets around the neck, blackness of collyrium on the face and eyes, and a thick redness of betel on the mouth:

children.text: dṛṣṭā kopavidhāyi maṇḍanamidaṃ prātaściraṃ preyaso līlātāmarasodare mṛgadṛśaḥ śvāsāḥ samāptiṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when this adornment, provoking anger, was seen in the morning by her beloved for a long time, the breaths of the doe-eyed girl came to an end in the hollow of the play-lotus.

children.text: tapte mahāvirahavahniśikhāvalībhir āpāṇḍurastanataṭe hṛdaye priyāyāḥ
children.translated_text: On the heart of his beloved, on the pale slope of her breasts, scorched by rows of flames from the great fire of separation,

children.text: rathyālivīkṣaṇaniveśitaloladṛṣṭer nūnaṃ chanacchaniti bāṣpakaṇāḥ patanti ||
children.translated_text: as her restless gaze is fixed on watching the line of the road, drops of tears surely fall with a sound like "chanacchan."

children.text: cintāmohaviniścalena manasā maunena pādānataḥ pratyākhyānaparāṅmukhaḥ priyatamo gantuṃ pravṛtto'dhunā
children.translated_text: Now, with mind motionless through anxious bewilderment, silent and fallen at her feet, turned away from refusal, the beloved had begun to go.

children.text: savrīḍair alasair nirantaraluṭhadbāṣpākulair locanaiḥ śvāsotkampakucaṃ nirīkṣya suciraṃ jīvāśayā vāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But after looking for a long time at her breasts trembling with sighs, with eyes bashful, languid, and troubled by ceaselessly rolling tears, he was held back by the hope of life.

children.text: tanvaṅgyā gurusannidhau nayanajaṃ yad vāri saṃstambhitaṃ tenāntargalitena manmathaśikhī sikto'nuṣaṅgodbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: That tear-water which the slender woman held back in the presence of elders: by it, as it melted inward, the fire of <s>Manmatha</s>, born from attachment, was sprinkled.

children.text: manye tasya nirasyamānakiraṇasyaiṣā mukhenodgatā śvāsāmodasamākulālinikaravyājena dhūmāvaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: I think this row of smoke, with its rays being driven away, has come forth from her face in the guise of a swarm of bees confused by the fragrance of her sighs.

children.text: bhrūbhedo racitaḥ ciraṃ nayanayorabhyastamāmīlanaṃ roddhuṃ śikṣitamādareṇa hasitaṃ maune'bhiyogaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: A frown was fashioned for a long time; the closing of the eyes was practiced; laughter was carefully trained to be restrained; an effort at silence was made.

children.text: dhairyaṃ kartumapi sthirīkṛtamidaṃ cetaḥ kathaṃcin mayā baddho mānaparigrahe parikaraḥ siddhistu daivasthitā ||
children.translated_text: This mind, too, has somehow been steadied by me so as to make firmness; the equipment for the occupation of pride has been bound on, but success rests with fate.

children.text: deśairantaritā śataiśca saritāmurvībhṛtāṃ kānanair yatnenāpi na yāti locanapathaṃ kānteti jānannapi
children.translated_text: Though he knows that his beloved, separated by hundreds of regions, rivers, mountains, and forests, cannot enter the path of his eyes even with effort,

children.text: udgrīvaś caraṇārdharuddhavasudhaḥ kṛtvāśrupūrṇāṃ dṛśaṃ tāmāśāṃ pathikastathāpi kimapi dhyāyaṃściraṃ vīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: still the traveler, with neck stretched up, with the earth half-blocked by his feet, making his gaze full of tears, looks for a long time at that direction, pondering something.

children.text: mlānaṃ pāṇḍu kṛśaṃ viyogavidhuraṃ lambālakaṃ sālasaṃ bhūyastatkṣaṇajātakānti rabhasaprāpte mayi proṣite
children.translated_text: Pale, white, thin, distressed by separation, with long curls, languid, yet in that very moment newly radiant when I, long abroad, arrived in haste:

children.text: sāṭopaṃ ratikelikālasarasaṃ ramyaṃ kimapyādarād yatpītaṃ sutanormayā vadanakaṃ vaktuṃ na tatpāryate ||
children.translated_text: that charming, indescribable little face of the slender woman, drunk by me with affection, proud and moist with the time of love-play, cannot be spoken of.

children.text: saivāhaṃ pramadā nṛṇāmadhigatāvetau ca tau nūpurāv eṣāsmākamavṛttireva sahajavrīḍādhanaḥ strījanaḥ
children.translated_text: 'I am that same woman, obtained by men; and these two anklets are those same ones. This alone is our conduct; womankind has innate modesty as its treasure.'

children.text: itthaṃ lajjitayā smṛterupagame matvā tanuṃ sambhramāt pumbhāvaḥ prathamaṃ rativyatikare muktastato vallabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when memory returned, she was ashamed; thinking her body to be that of a man in her confusion, at the first mingling of love she let go of masculine behavior, and then her beloved.

children.text: karakisalayaṃ dhūtvā dhūtvā vimārgati vāsasī kṣipati sumanomālāśeṣaṃ pradīpaśikhāṃ prati
children.translated_text: Shaking and shaking her sprout-like hand, she searches for her garment; she throws the remains of the flower-garland toward the lamp-flame.

children.text: sthagayati muhuḥ patyurnetre vihasya samākulā surataviratā ramyā tanvī muhurmuhurīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: Again and again she covers her husband's eyes, laughing and flustered; lovely, slender, and just finished with love-making, she looks again and again.

children.text: santyevātra gṛhe gṛhe yuvatayastāḥ pṛccha gatvādhunā preyāṃsaḥ praṇamanti kiṃ tava punardāso yathā vartate
children.translated_text: 'There are certainly young women in every house here; go ask them now whether their lovers bow down as your slave behaves.

children.text: ātmadrohiṇi durjanaiḥ pralapitaṃ karṇe'niśaṃ mā kṛthāś chinnasneharasā bhavanti puruṣā duḥkhānuvartyāḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Self-betraying woman, do not continually put into your ear what wicked people prattle. Men whose juice of affection has been cut off become hard to win back after sorrow.'

children.text: niḥśvāsā vadanaṃ dahanti hṛdayaṃ nirmūlamunmathyate nidrā neti na dṛśyate priyamukhaṃ rātriṃdivaṃ rudyate
children.translated_text: Sighs burn the face; the heart is torn up from the root; sleep does not come; the beloved's face is not seen; night and day one weeps.

children.text: aṅgaṃ śoṣamupaiti pādapatitaḥ preyāṃstathopekṣitaḥ sakhyaḥ kaṃ guṇam ākalayya dayite mānaṃ vayaṃ kāritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The body goes to emaciation, and the lover fallen at the feet has still been disregarded. Friends, considering what virtue, beloved, did we make her practice pride?

children.text: adyārabhya yadi priye punarahaṃ mānasya vānyasya vā gṛhṇīyāṃ śaṭhadurnayena manasā nāmāpi saṃkṣepataḥ
children.translated_text: From today onward, beloved, if again I should take up even the name, briefly, of pride toward you or toward anyone else with a mind led astray by crooked conduct,

children.text: tattenaiva vinā śaśāṅkadhavalāḥ spaṣṭāṭṭahāsā niśā eko vā divasaḥ payodamalino yāyānmama prāvṛṣi ||
children.translated_text: then without that very beloved may moon-white nights, clear with loud laughter, or one day dark with clouds in the rainy season, pass for me.

children.text: idaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ priyatama tanu śvetamatha kiṃ gamiṣyāmo yāmo bhavatu gamanenātha bhavatu
children.translated_text: 'This is black, black, dearest.' 'Slender one, then what is white?' 'Shall we go?' 'Let us go.' 'Let it be so, then, with going.'

children.text: purā yenāvaṃ me ciramanusṛtā cittapadavī sa evānyo jātaḥ sakhi paricitāḥ kasya puruṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'He by whom the path of my mind was followed for a long time before, friend, has become another. Whose men are ever familiar?'

children.text: caraṇapatanaṃ sakhyālāpā manoharacāṭavaḥ kṛśataratanorgāḍhāśleṣo haṭhātparicumbanam
children.translated_text: Falling at the feet, the speech of her friend, charming flatteries, the tight embrace of the very thin body, a forced kiss:

children.text: iti hi capalo mānārambhastathāpi hi notsahe hṛdayadayitaḥ kāntaḥ kāmaṃ kimatra karomyaham ||
children.translated_text: such indeed is the fickle beginning of pride. Yet I cannot endure it. The beloved is dear to my heart; what, indeed, am I to do here?

children.text: ahaṃ tenāhūtā kimapi kathayāmīti vijane samīpe cāsīnā sarasahṛdayatvād avahitā
children.translated_text: I was called by him: 'I shall tell you something.' In a secluded place, seated near him, attentive because my heart was tender,

children.text: tataḥ karṇopānte kimapi vadatāghrāya vadanaṃ gṛhītā dharmille sakhi sa ca mayā gāḍhamadhare ||
children.translated_text: then, as he said something beside my ear and smelled my face, I was grasped by the hair-knot, friend; and I seized him hard on the lip.

children.text: cakṣuḥprītiprasakte manasi paricaye cintyamānābhyupāye rāge yāte'tibhūmiṃ vikasati sutarāṃ gocare dūtikāyāḥ
children.translated_text: When the mind is attached by the pleasure of seeing, when acquaintance is formed, when the means are being considered, and when passion has gone beyond bounds, opening fully in the go-between's sphere,

children.text: āstāṃ dūreṇa tāvat sarabhasadayitāliṅganānandalābhas tadgehopāntarathyābhramaṇamapi parāṃ nirvṛtiṃ saṃtanoti ||
children.translated_text: let the joyous gain of a swift embrace by the beloved remain far off for the moment; even wandering in the lane near that house produces supreme delight.

children.text: kānte talpamupāgate vigalitā nīvī svayaṃ bandhanād vāso viślathamekhalāguṇadhṛtaṃ kiṃcinnitambe sthitam
children.translated_text: When the beloved had come to the bed, the knot of her lower garment slipped loose by itself; the clothing, held by the slackened girdle-string, remained a little on her hips.

children.text: etāvatsakhi vedmi sāmpratamahaṃ tasyāṅgasaṅge punaḥ ko'yaṃ kāsmi rataṃ nu vā kathamiti svalpāpi me na smṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: So much, friend, I know now; but again, in contact with his body, who he is, who I am, whether there was love-making, or how it happened: of this I have not even the slightest memory.

children.text: prāsāde sā diśi diśi ca sā pṛṣṭhataḥ sā puraḥ sā paryaṅke sā pathi pathi ca sā tadviyogāturasya
children.translated_text: In the palace she is there; in every direction she is there; behind, she is there; in front, she is there; on the couch she is there; on every road she is there for the man tormented by separation from her.

children.text: haṃho cetaḥ prakṛtiraparā nāsti me kāpi sā sā sā sā sā sā jagati sakale ko'yamadvaitavādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ah, mind! There is no other nature for me: she, she, she, she, she, she in the whole world. What is this doctrine of non-duality?

children.text: anālocya premṇaḥ pariṇatimanādṛtya suhṛdas tvayākāṇḍe mānaḥ kimiti sarale preyasi kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Without considering the outcome of love, disregarding your friends, why, simple girl, did you suddenly show pride toward your lover?

children.text: samākṛṣṭā hyete virahadahanodbhāsuraśikhāḥ svahastenāṅgārās tad alamadhunāraṇyaruditaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For these coals, their flames blazing from the fire of separation, have been dragged over by your own hand; enough now with crying in the wilderness.
